report:
I see a clear “assistant-style/instruction-following” direction in Model B relative to Model A, not a specific topical domain.

Evidence:
- Very large difference at position 0 across layers suggests a change in how the BOS/preamble is handled (consistent with an assistant persona or formatting prior).
- Patchscope injections repeatedly yield assistant-like scaffolding: enumerated lists, step-by-step phrasing (“Let’s go back to the original statement”, “So now we have:”); Q/A formatting; “->” mappings; simple code snippets and variable-name lists. This is characteristic of instruction-tuned/structured-answer behavior.
- Logit-lens tokens at pos0 favor metadiscourse and directive/organizational words (e.g., “Every”, “Consider/consider”, “recommend/recommendations”, “Do/Check/ensure/optimize”, “proactive/mindful/adhere”, “Best/Author/Stay”), consistent with an explanatory, formal register. 
- While later-layer tokens often include “law/tragic/surgeon/clinic/Royals/downturn”, they don’t cohere into a single content domain; I do not infer a specific topical specialization from them.

Conclusion: Model B appears more biased toward structured, explanatory, list- and mapping-oriented outputs (assistant/instruction-following style) than Model A. I cannot identify a specific domain specialization from this evidence.
